lines.text: You can travel with your own transport [vervoer] (bicycle, scooter, car) or with public transport [openbaar vervoer]: train, bus, tram or metro.
Sometimes you have to combine [combineren] types of public transport and transfer [overstappen], for example from the train to the metro.
You can plan [plannen] your journey with an app or on the internet.
For example the app of the NS (Nederlandse Spoorwegen) for the train: you fill in two stations.
Or the app of 9292: you fill in two addresses.
You can also enter when you want to depart [vertrekken] or arrive [aankomen].
Then you get suggestions with times and prices, and information about transfers.
Sometimes public transport has a delay [vertraging] — you can also see that in the app.
To travel by public transport, you need a card.
There must always be sufficient balance [voldoende saldo] on your card.
You can also travel with your bank card [bankpas].
Before your journey you must check in [inchecken]: you hold your card against a post [paal].
After your journey you must check out [uitchecken].
The posts are in the bus, at stations or on platforms.
Then you pay more than necessary.
If you travel often, you can buy a subscription [abonnement].
Do you usually travel outside rush hour [spits]?
Then you can buy an off-peak card [dalurenkaart].
